hero.headline: House rejects extension of surveillance law set to expire
hero.body:
The House of Representatives failed to pass a short-term extension of a powerful surveillance law, clearing the way for a key intelligence authority to lapse. The measure fell short in a 198-218 vote on Thursday, with Democrats blocking the renewal of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) in protest of a controversial Trump administration appointment.

The dispute centers on Donald Trump's decision to name Bill Pulte as acting director of national intelligence. Pulte, a major Republican donor and head of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, has no extensive national security experience, according to House Democrats. The law explicitly requires the intelligence director to have "extensive" national security experience.

"Bill Pulte has no relevant national security experience. Consequently, his appointment is in defiance of the law," said House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries and other senior Democrats in a statement. They argued the appointment demonstrates Pulte's willingness to misuse government databases to target Trump's political opponents.

Section 702 of FISA, enacted after 9/11, allows U.S. intelligence agencies to intercept foreign communications without a court warrant. Republican leaders had been negotiating a compromise with Democrats and civil liberties-minded members of their own party to extend the law for three years. Those negotiations collapsed after the Pulte announcement.

"There is a path to reauthorizing FISA, but it will require enacting meaningful reforms," Democrats said, explaining their opposition to what they called "kicking the can further down the road."

Republicans attempted to pass the extension through a fast-track process requiring a two-thirds majority. They fell significantly short, with 19 Republican members joining most Democrats in opposition. The Senate had already rejected a similar extension attempt the previous week, with all Democrats except John Fetterman of Pennsylvania voting no, alongside seven conservative Republicans concerned about civil liberties implications.

However, the surveillance program will not completely shut down. The FISA court issued a year-long certification allowing Section 702 collection to continue through approximately March 2027, even if the law itself lapses. The statute contains provisions permitting collection to continue under that court order despite the law's expiration.

Still, the failure to extend FISA creates uncertainty about intelligence operations. Republican leaders of the Senate intelligence and judiciary committees sent a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio asking the administration to prepare for "a potential significant gap in foreign intelligence collection."

Lawmakers will need to resolve the situation when they return, either through retroactive authorization or new legislation that can gain bipartisan support. The outcome will determine how intelligence agencies conduct surveillance operations and their access to key investigative tools.

cards.headline: Trump Threatens Further Strikes on Iran as Military Exchanges Escalate
cards.body:
President Trump announced that U.S. forces would strike Iran again on Thursday evening and threatened to seize control of Kharg Island, a critical hub for Iran's oil exports. The threat came as the two countries exchanged fire for the second consecutive day despite a ceasefire agreement that has largely stalled.

The escalation marks a dangerous shift in the fragile peace arrangement reached in April. Trump posted on Truth Social that the U.S. would hit Iran "VERY HARD, TONIGHT," claiming that most of Iran's offensive capacity had already been destroyed. He also stated that the U.S. would take Kharg Island, which handles approximately 90 percent of Iran's oil exports and contains vast storage facilities. Control of the island would severely damage Iran's ability to sell crude oil on international markets.

The current round of military exchanges began with Israeli airstrikes on Iran following Iranian missile attacks on northern Israel. The Israeli military struck Iranian petrochemical facilities and defense systems across multiple cities including Isfahan, Karaj, Tabriz and Tehran. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps responded by targeting two military bases in Israel as part of Operation Nasr, or "Victory."

Tensions have risen further with Yemen's Houthi rebels, aligned with Iran, announcing they would ban Israeli maritime navigation in the Red Sea and target Israeli-affiliated ships. This escalation threatens disruptions to a crucial global trade route.

Trump reportedly urged Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu not to retaliate immediately after the Iranian missile attack, telling him the U.S. would handle the situation. However, Israel proceeded with strikes anyway. Iranian officials rejected suggestions that Netanyahu defied Trump's wishes, instead claiming that no Israeli military action occurs without U.S. coordination and approval. The White House did not respond to questions about whether the strikes were coordinated with the U.S.

The conflict has already impacted global markets and prices. Brent crude jumped 3.50 dollars to 96.59 dollars per barrel following Monday's exchanges. Stocks in Asia, heavily dependent on oil imports, fell sharply in early trading. Within the United States, inflation has risen to 4.2 percent in May, a three-year high, with gas prices averaging about 4.16 dollars per gallon, roughly one dollar higher than a year earlier. Trump responded to inflation concerns by stating "I love the inflation," suggesting he was not worried about price increases.

Stalled negotiations to convert the ceasefire into a permanent peace agreement remain a major concern. Iran seeks the lifting of international sanctions and control over the Strait of Hormuz, while Trump demands any deal must prevent Iran from developing nuclear weapons, a claim Iran disputes. The situation has drawn international concern about broader regional destabilization and the potential for full-scale war in the Middle East.

cards.headline: Trump says US will not renew trade agreement with Canada and Mexico
cards.teaser: The president indicated he is not looking to renew the USMCA trade deal, signaling a shift toward yearly reviews.
cards.body:
Trump announced the United States will not renew the USMCA trade agreement with Canada and Mexico, suggesting instead that the deal would face yearly reviews. The statement marks a departure from the three-country trade framework established during his first term.

Trump's ambassador to Canada identified specific needs America has from its northern neighbor. Analysts suggest Trump is unlikely to completely abandon the trade framework, pointing to economic interdependencies between the three nations.

cards.headline: Israel Plans Rapid Expansion of West Bank Settlements Ahead of Elections
cards.teaser: The Israeli government is rushing to install temporary housing at about 60 empty sites in the occupied West Bank before national elections this fall.
cards.body:
Israel Set to Rapidly Expand West Bank Settlement

Israel announced plans to accelerate settlement expansion in the occupied West Bank, with temporary housing to be installed at approximately 60 currently empty sites before national elections this fall.

The government is using temporary structures to establish physical presence across multiple locations simultaneously. This rapid deployment strategy could make future removal more difficult, potentially locking in settlement presence regardless of election outcomes.

cards.headline: Toronto Police Officer Killed During Raid Tied to U.S. Consulate Shooting
cards.teaser: A Toronto police officer died after being shot while investigating a March shooting outside the U.S. consulate.
cards.body:
A Toronto police officer has been fatally shot while conducting a raid on an apartment linked to a March attack on the U.S. consulate. Constable Marc Pinizzotto, 43, was killed during an early-morning search warrant in the city's northwest. He was taken to a hospital where he later died from his injuries.

Police Chief Myron Demkiw confirmed the incident was connected to the earlier consulate shooting. A 19-year-old suspect remains at large following the officer's death.

cards.headline: Medicare Advantage Plans Frequently Deny Seniors Access to Nursing Home Care
cards.teaser: Federal investigators found Medicare Advantage plans routinely reject requests for short-term nursing home or inpatient services.
cards.body:
Two reports by U.S. investigators revealed that Medicare Advantage plans frequently deny seniors access to short-term nursing home care and inpatient services. The analysis highlights systematic issues with how private insurers handle coverage requests for specialized medical care.

The findings raise questions about how Medicare Advantage plans, which are privately run alternatives to traditional Medicare, make coverage decisions. The reports document patterns of quick rejections for services that may be medically necessary, affecting seniors' ability to access care following hospital stays or during recovery periods.

cards.headline: Multiple countries move to ban social media access for children
cards.teaser: Australia led a wave of nations restricting youth access to social platforms, aiming to reduce cyberbullying, addiction, and predator exposure.
cards.body:
Several countries have implemented or are considering bans on social media use by children following Australia's pioneering restriction in late 2025. The policies aim to protect young users from cyberbullying, social media addiction, and contact with online predators.

Australia became the first nation to enact such a ban, establishing a model other countries are now examining. The restrictions target the risks that social platforms pose to minors, including psychological pressures and safety threats inherent in online social environments.

cards.headline: U.S. Confirms Third Strike on Indian-Crewed Tankers This Week
cards.teaser: Three Indian sailors were killed in U.S. strikes on oil tankers, prompting India to issue a strong protest and demand an end to attacks on ships.
cards.body:
The United States confirmed it carried out a third strike on oil tankers with Indian crew members this week. Three Indian sailors were killed in the attacks, which targeted vessels off the coast of Oman. India has lodged a formal protest with U.S. authorities over the incidents.

The Indian government voiced strong objections to the strikes and called for an immediate end to attacks on commercial shipping vessels. The tankers were struck as part of ongoing U.S. military operations in the region, though the specific circumstances of each strike were not fully disclosed by American officials.

cards.headline: Nigeria Evacuates Citizens from South Africa as Anti-Migrant Sentiment Grows
cards.teaser: Nigeria has begun repatriating its citizens from South Africa following reports of xenophobic attacks against foreign nationals.
cards.body:
Nigeria started evacuating its citizens from South Africa in response to rising anti-migrant sentiment and reports of xenophobic violence. The country is the latest African nation to repatriate citizens from South Africa amid growing tensions over immigration.

The decision to evacuate follows accounts of attacks targeting foreign nationals in South Africa. Several other African countries have taken similar steps in recent weeks to bring their citizens home as concerns about safety have mounted.

cards.headline: Global Refugee Numbers Drop Slightly but Most Return to Unstable Conditions
cards.teaser: The U.N. reported nearly 118 million forcibly displaced people in 2025, a slight decrease from the previous year, but many returnees face turmoil at home.
cards.body:
The number of forcibly displaced people worldwide stood at nearly 118 million in 2025, representing a small decline from the previous year, according to the United Nations refugee agency. Despite the decrease, the U.N. noted that many refugees who returned home faced continued instability and difficult conditions.

The slight drop in displacement numbers came after years of increases driven by conflicts, persecution, and violence around the world. The U.N. report highlighted concerns about the circumstances awaiting those who returned to their countries of origin, suggesting the reduction in displacement may not reflect genuine improvements in safety.

cards.headline: Drone Strike Kills Civilians at Funeral in Sudan
cards.teaser: Rights groups accuse the RSF paramilitary of targeting a funeral procession in el-Obeid, a city on the front line of Sudan's civil war.
cards.body:
A drone strike hit a funeral procession in el-Obeid, Sudan, killing civilians gathered for the ceremony. Human rights groups have accused the Rapid Support Forces paramilitary group of carrying out the attack.

El-Obeid sits on the front line of Sudan's ongoing civil war, where the RSF and rival forces have engaged in intense fighting. The strike on a civilian funeral demonstrates how the conflict has increasingly affected non-combatants in contested areas.

cards.headline: Pentagon partially evacuated after hazardous materials sensor triggers false alarm
cards.teaser: Firefighters responded to the Pentagon after a sensor detected a potential air quality issue, prompting a partial evacuation and shelter-in-place order.
cards.body:
The Pentagon's security systems detected an air quality issue, triggering an alert that prompted an immediate response from hazmat teams, firefighters, and police. The building was locked down and partially evacuated as emergency responders arrived to investigate the reported problem.

After assessing the situation, officials determined the sensor had produced a false alarm and there was no actual hazardous materials threat present. Some Pentagon workers sheltered in place during the investigation.

cards.headline: Man pleads guilty to killing Minnesota lawmaker and her husband
cards.teaser: A man who posed as an officer admitted to killing a top Minnesota Democrat and her husband in a federal case.
cards.body:
Vance Boelter pleaded guilty in federal court to murdering Melissa Hortman, the Minnesota House Speaker, and her husband Mark Hortman. He also faced charges for shooting state senator John Hoffman and his wife Yvette in nonfatal attacks. Boelter disguised himself as a police officer and drove a fake squad car when he came to their doors in the early hours of June 14, 2025.

Boelter changed his plea after prosecutors agreed not to pursue the death penalty, allowing him to avoid a capital trial.

cards.headline: Opening of bridge connecting US and Canada delayed
cards.teaser: The launch of the Gordie Howe International Bridge between Detroit and Canada has been postponed again.
cards.body:
Officials announced another delay in opening the Gordie Howe International Bridge, a long-awaited crossing between the United States and Canada. The bridge project has faced multiple postponements beyond its original timeline.

Canadian official Mark Carney stated the opening may take a little longer than previously anticipated. The bridge has been the subject of political attention, with Trump previously threatening to block its opening during trade disputes.

cards.headline: House Republicans meet with defense secretary over budget demands
cards.teaser: Republican lawmakers gathered with Defense Secretary Hegseth following Trump's push for additional reconciliation legislation.
cards.body:
House Republicans met with Defense Secretary Hegseth following Trump's push for a third reconciliation bill that would include the Save America Act. The administration is advancing its legislative priorities through these discussions.

However, top Republican appropriators have rejected the idea of a third reconciliation bill. Senator Collins also expressed concerns about Air Force funding plans that could impact F-35 engine production in Maine.

cards.headline: Taiwan opposition leader says talks with Xi avoided reunification discussion
cards.teaser: A Taiwanese opposition figure reported that a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping did not include discussion of reunification.
cards.body:
Cheng, a Taiwan opposition leader, stated that his meeting with Xi Jinping steered clear of talks about reunification between China and Taiwan. The comments come at a time of heightened attention to cross-strait relations.

Taiwan is awaiting approval on a $14 billion arms package from the United States. Uncertainty persists over Washington's long-term commitment to Taiwan's defense as the island navigates its relationship with both Beijing and the US.

cards.headline: Trump says US will strike Iran and threatens seizure of key oil hub
cards.teaser: The president announced plans for military action against Iran and threatened to take control of Kharg Island and oil infrastructure.
cards.body:
Trump has threatened to launch military strikes against Iran and seize control of Kharg Island, a critical oil hub that handles roughly 90% of Iran's oil exports. The threat comes as negotiations aimed at converting a temporary ceasefire into a lasting peace agreement have stalled for weeks, with both sides trading blame over ceasefire violations and continuing limited strikes.

The two countries remain at odds over key issues. Iran is seeking the lifting of international sanctions, unfreezing of billions in frozen assets, and control over the Strait of Hormuz. Trump has insisted any peace deal must prevent Iran from developing nuclear weapons, while Tehran denies pursuing nuclear development.

hero.headline: European Central Bank Raises Interest Rates as Inflation Accelerates
hero.body:
The European Central Bank raised its main deposit rate from 2% to 2.25%, marking its first rate increase since 2023. Financial markets anticipate two additional rises by next spring as the central bank confronts surging inflation linked to the ongoing war in Iran.

Eurozone consumer price inflation climbed to 3.2% in May 2026, up from 3% in April, well above the ECB's 2% target. The conflict in the Middle East has disrupted energy supplies and pushed oil prices above $90 per barrel, compared with roughly $70 before the war began. Energy costs are now feeding through to broader price pressures as manufacturers and retailers seek to maintain profit margins.

The ECB also raised its main refinancing rate to 2.4% from 2.15%. The decision represents a shift in strategy after the central bank held rates steady in hopes that the United States and Iran would reach a peace agreement. That outcome has not materialized, forcing policymakers to act.

ECB President Christine Lagarde acknowledged the uncertainty surrounding the conflict's economic impact. "The full implication of the war for medium-term inflation and growth will depend on the intensity and duration of the energy price shock, as well as the scale of its indirect and second-round effects," she said.

The move comes after criticism that the ECB delayed rate increases in 2022 following Russia's invasion of Ukraine, allowing inflation to become more entrenched. Officials had considered "looking through" the initial energy price spike from the Middle East conflict, but mounting evidence that higher oil and gas prices were already accelerating inflation prompted the change in approach.

The central bank trimmed its growth forecasts for the eurozone to 0.8% in 2026 and 1.2% in 2027, down from previous projections of 0.9% and 1.3%. "The risks to the growth outlook are to the downside, mainly owing to the war in the Middle East, which has added to the volatile global policy environment," Lagarde stated, warning that prolonged energy supply disruptions could push prices higher for longer than currently expected.

Mark Wall, chief European economist at Deutsche Bank, called this a significant moment. "Not only is this the first ECB hike since 2023, it is also the first hike by one of the major global central banks in response to the energy shock," he said. However, Wall cautioned that markets may be overestimating the rate-hiking cycle. He predicted one additional increase in September but not the multiple hikes markets were pricing in, given weakness in employment and growth.

The Bank of England is expected to hold rates at 3.75% at its next meeting, while the Federal Reserve is also anticipated to pause despite the highest inflation in the G7 at 4.2%.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Swing on Renewed U.S.-Iran Conflict
cards.teaser: Oil markets reacted to a second day of military exchanges between the United States and Iran.
cards.body:
The United States launched air strikes on Iran for a second consecutive day, prompting oil prices to jump as markets reacted to escalating tensions between the two countries. The renewed military exchanges have heightened concerns about a potential return to open conflict.

Traders are monitoring the situation closely due to fears that continued confrontation could disrupt oil supplies from the region and affect global energy markets.

cards.headline: Elon Musk's Net Worth Falls More Than $50 Billion
cards.teaser: The decline comes ahead of SpaceX's planned initial public offering.
cards.body:
Elon Musk's net worth has declined by more than $50 billion. As the world's richest person, Musk leads X, Tesla, and SpaceX.

The timing of this decline coincides with SpaceX's anticipated initial public offering, which is expected to be among the largest technology IPOs in recent years. The public listing will establish a new valuation benchmark for the aerospace company.

cards.headline: Oracle Shares Drop After Earnings Report
cards.teaser: Investors reacted negatively to the company's increased spending plans and debt levels.
cards.body:
Oracle shares fell 11 percent following the company's earnings announcement, which disclosed substantial capital raising plans that sparked investor concerns. The decline comes as the broader stock market rose, with the Dow and S&P 500 gaining ground after wholesale inflation data and a tech sector rebound.

The sell-off reflects worries about Oracle's increased spending and cash position. However, some analysts view the post-earnings dip as a buying opportunity, arguing that the company's cloud infrastructure investments are essential for long-term competitiveness.

cards.headline: Chinese Dominance in Robot Manufacturing Presents Challenge for Competitors
cards.teaser: Companies in China produce robot components at scale and prices other nations struggle to match.
cards.body:
Building robots without relying on Chinese suppliers has become nearly impossible for manufacturers worldwide. Chinese companies have leveraged the country's electric vehicle industry to produce robot parts at a scale and price point that competitors cannot match.

The manufacturing advantage stems from established supply chains and production capacity developed for the automotive sector. This dominance in component manufacturing gives Chinese robotics companies a significant edge in the growing automation industry, making it difficult for manufacturers in other countries to compete on cost.

cards.headline: Lee Raymond, Former Exxon Mobil Chief, Dies at 87
cards.teaser: He oversaw the creation of the merged oil giant and was known for denying climate science.
cards.body:
Lee Raymond, who led the merger that created oil giant Exxon Mobil, died at age 87. During his tenure as chief executive, he oversaw the acquisition that combined Exxon and Mobil into one of the world's largest energy companies.

Raymond was known for aggressive cost-cutting measures and for publicly denying the scientific consensus on climate change. His leadership shaped the modern oil industry and influenced how major energy companies responded to environmental concerns during a critical period.

hero.headline: Extreme rainfall killed 7% of world's rarest orangutans, study finds
hero.body:
Four days of intense rainfall and landslides killed 7% of the world's rarest orangutan population, according to a new study examining the impact of extreme weather on the critically endangered Tapanuli orangutan. The research provides concrete evidence of how climate change-induced weather events pose immediate threats to species already facing habitat loss and fragmentation.

The study focused on the Tapanuli orangutan, of which only about 800 individuals remain. Researchers found that more than 1,000 millimeters of rain fell over four days in North Sumatra province in November 2025, killing an estimated 58 orangutans. This represents 11% of the local population and 7% of the entire species. Scientists used satellite imagery overlaid with ape density estimates to determine how Cyclone Senyar affected orangutans living in the West Block of the Batang Toru ecosystem.

The rainfall triggered catastrophic landslides that destroyed approximately 8,300 hectares, or 11.7%, of this critical forest habitat. According to the research, human-induced climate change caused by fossil fuel burning increased the rainfall intensity by up to 50%.

Tapanuli orangutans face multiple threats beyond extreme weather. The Batang Toru ecosystem where they live is already threatened by mining operations, palm oil plantations, and a large hydropower project. These pressures, combined with the sudden demographic shock from the extreme weather event, raise serious concerns about the species' survival.

"It is tragic to lose so many apes in this way. In landscapes where populations are small and fragmented, this type of weather or climate event can have population-level consequences. It is extremely worrying for the future of this ape," said Serge Wich, a primatologist at Liverpool John Moores University and study co-author.

Previous research suggests that annual losses of just 1% of the Tapanuli orangutan population would eventually lead to extinction. The loss of 58 individuals in a single event represents a devastating demographic shock that conservation programs struggle to address.

Conservation biologist Jatna Supriatna from Universitas Indonesia emphasized the urgency of action: "To prevent the first modern extinction of a great ape species, Indonesia must permanently protect the Batang Toru ecosystem, but our international partners must also meet their global commitments by providing immediate biodiversity-recovery financing."

In response, the Indonesian government has temporarily paused all major industrial activity in the Batang Toru area to allow scientists to investigate how best to secure the long-term survival of the species while assessing risks to human lives. Researchers involved in the study recommended an immediate moratorium on land-use activities that degrade remaining orangutan habitat and the expansion of protected areas to stabilize the population.

cards.headline: DoorDash launches AI chatbot for natural language ordering
cards.teaser: The delivery app introduces a feature that lets users search for food and products using conversational prompts and photos instead of browsing menus.
cards.body:
DoorDash introduced Ask DoorDash, an AI chatbot that lets users order by describing what they want in conversational language rather than browsing menus manually. The tool accepts both text prompts and photos, enabling customers to search for items through natural queries instead of scrolling through restaurants and stores to build their cart.

The chatbot interprets customer requests and translates them into searchable products and menu items across the platform, streamlining the ordering process.

cards.headline: Deezer introduces tool to detect AI-generated music across streaming platforms
cards.teaser: The music service launched a scanner that identifies AI-created tracks in playlists from Spotify, Apple Music, and other competing platforms.
cards.body:
Deezer has released a tool that identifies AI-generated music in playlists across multiple streaming platforms, including Spotify and Apple Music. The scanner allows users to analyze their existing collections and determine which tracks were created by artificial intelligence.

As AI-generated music becomes increasingly common on streaming services, the tool offers listeners a new way to curate their listening experience and distinguish between human-created and algorithm-generated content.

cards.headline: Waymo launches subscription program with cash back and cancellation perks
cards.teaser: The autonomous vehicle service introduced a monthly membership offering benefits including a 10% rebate on rides and no-penalty cancellations.
cards.body:
Waymo Premier is a new loyalty program that costs $29.99 per month. Subscribers receive 10% cash back on rides and can cancel trips without incurring fees.

The subscription service reflects Waymo's effort to build a stable customer base for its autonomous vehicle service. The program's benefits are designed to encourage regular use of the self-driving taxi platform.

cards.headline: Microsoft signs carbon removal deal with Indian startup Alt Carbon
cards.teaser: The tech giant selected the India-based company for carbon credits after more than a year of scientific review, marking India's expanding role in climate technology.
cards.body:
Microsoft has partnered with Alt Carbon, an Indian carbon removal startup, after conducting over a year of scientific review and due diligence. The agreement included additional verification measures and data-sharing protocols beyond typical arrangements.

The deal underscores India's expanding role in the carbon removal sector. Microsoft's decision to work with Alt Carbon demonstrates growing confidence in climate technology innovators from emerging markets, supported by rigorous oversight mechanisms to validate carbon credit quality.

cards.headline: Endurance Energy secures $54 million for ocean geothermal project
cards.teaser: A startup founded by SpaceX alumni raised funding to develop technology extracting geothermal energy from the ocean.
cards.body:
Endurance Energy, led by former SpaceX executive Andrew Redd, raised $54 million to develop ocean-based geothermal energy extraction. The company aims to tap what Redd describes as vast amounts of untapped thermal energy in ocean waters.

The funding supports technology designed to harness geothermal resources from marine environments. The approach differs from traditional geothermal energy production, which typically relies on drilling into underground heat sources on land.

cards.headline: New app sorts screenshots into searchable collections
cards.teaser: Pool's application organizes saved screenshots, retrieves original links, and helps users rediscover saved recipes, products, and travel ideas.
cards.body:
Pool's new app automatically organizes screenshots into personalized collections while recovering the original web links behind saved images. This makes it easier to rediscover and revisit content you've captured.

The app sorts screenshots into categories like products, recipes, and travel ideas—solving the frustration of accumulating hundreds of screenshots with no easy way to find them again. By connecting images to their source links, the app transforms scattered screenshots into a searchable, organized system.

hero.headline: Tarik Skubal returns to Tigers rotation six weeks after elbow surgery
hero.teaser: Detroit Tigers ace Tarik Skubal will start Saturday against Cleveland, returning less than six weeks after undergoing elbow surgery.
hero.body:
Tarik Skubal will take the mound Saturday when the Detroit Tigers face the Cleveland Guardians, marking the left-hander's return to action. The Tigers ace underwent elbow surgery less than six weeks ago, making his recovery timeline notably swift.

Skubal's return provides a significant boost to Detroit's rotation as they continue their season. The left-hander has been a cornerstone of the Tigers pitching staff, and his absence left a void that the team struggled to fill during his recovery period.

cards.headline: Knicks complete largest comeback in NBA Finals history, move within one win of title
cards.teaser: The New York Knicks pulled off the largest comeback in NBA Finals history Wednesday night, erasing a 29-point second-half deficit to defeat the San Antonio Spur.
cards.body:
The New York Knicks mounted a historic comeback in Game 4 of the NBA Finals, erasing a 29-point second-half deficit to defeat the San Antonio Spurs. OG Anunoby finished the improbable turnaround with a tip-in that brought the Knicks within one win of their first championship since 1973.

The Spurs controlled the game through three quarters before New York rallied in the fourth period. With the victory, the Knicks can clinch the title with a win in Game 5, bringing the franchise closer to ending its championship drought that has lasted over 50 years.

cards.headline: Jalen Hurts addresses A.J. Brown trade as Eagles move forward
cards.teaser: Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts spoke publicly about the A.J. Brown trade for the first time since it became official Wednesday.
cards.body:
Jalen Hurts addressed the A.J. Brown trade for the first time since it became official Wednesday. The Eagles quarterback reflected on what they accomplished together over their four years in Philadelphia before shifting his attention ahead.

The departure marks a significant change for the Eagles offense as the team prepares for the upcoming season.

cards.headline: Dodgers squander five-run lead as Shohei Ohtani questions missed challenge
cards.teaser: The Pirates rallied from five runs down to defeat the Dodgers 9-8 after Shohei Ohtani missed an automated ball-strike challenge in the seventh inning.
cards.body:
Shohei Ohtani pitched effectively through six innings Wednesday before the Dodgers' defense crumbled in the seventh. Los Angeles squandered a five-run advantage as the Pittsburgh Pirates mounted a comeback, ultimately winning 9-8.

A missed automated ball-strike challenge during the Pirates' rally proved costly for the Dodgers. Ohtani expressed regret over not using the challenge to contest a call, a decision that allowed Pittsburgh to maintain momentum and complete their comeback.

cards.headline: Serena Williams doubles return cut short by partner's injury
cards.teaser: Serena Williams' return to competitive tennis ended prematurely after doubles partner Victoria Mboko withdrew from the HSBC Championships with a knee injury.
cards.body:
Serena Williams' comeback tournament has ended prematurely at Queen's Club. Her doubles partner Victoria Mboko withdrew after sustaining a knee injury during her singles match when she slipped on the grass court.

Williams had made a successful return to competition at age 44 after a four-year absence, winning her opening doubles match with Mboko against third seeds Nicole Melichar Martinez and Erin Routliffe. The pair were set to face Leylah Fernandez and Laura Siegemund in their next round before Mboko's injury forced her out of the tournament.

cards.headline: Wimbledon increases prize money by 20 percent after player pressure
cards.teaser: Wimbledon announced a 20 percent increase in total prize money and singles champion payouts following calls from players for greater revenue sharing.
cards.body:
Wimbledon has announced a record 20 percent increase in prize money, raising the total purse to £64.2 million. Singles champions will receive £3.6 million, while first-round losers will earn £80,000. The increase applies across all rounds of competition.

The announcement comes amid ongoing player demands for a larger share of tournament revenues, particularly following disputes that emerged after the French Open. However, the All England Club's increase may still fall short of appeasing top players' compensation demands.

cards.headline: Lions defensive back Brian Branch continues Achilles recovery without timetable
cards.teaser: Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell says defensive back Brian Branch is progressing well from an Achilles tear but will not commit to a return timeline.
cards.body:
Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell provided an update on defensive back Brian Branch's Achilles injury recovery, saying the player is "doing well." However, Campbell made clear the team will not rush Branch's return to the field.

The coach declined to establish any specific timeline for when Branch will be available to play, emphasizing the Lions' cautious approach to his rehabilitation from the significant injury.

hero.headline: Lionsgate Takes Equity Stake in AI Video Company Runway
hero.body:
Lionsgate has acquired an equity stake in Runway, a generative AI video company, and plans to use its existing film and TV franchises to create AI-generated short-form series. The move expands a partnership the two companies first established in 2024 and represents a significant commitment by the studio to artificial intelligence technology in entertainment production.

The expanded partnership will see Lionsgate and Runway begin developing AI-powered content drawn from the studio's catalog of intellectual properties. This approach allows the studio to leverage its existing franchises for new formats and distribution channels using generative AI tools that can create video content from text prompts and other inputs.

The equity investment deepens the financial and strategic relationship between the traditional Hollywood studio and the AI technology provider. Runway has emerged as one of the leading companies in generative AI video, competing in a space that has attracted significant attention and investment as studios and content creators explore how artificial intelligence might transform production processes and content creation.

The plan to create short-form series from existing franchises suggests Lionsgate sees AI as a tool for expanding the reach and longevity of its intellectual property rather than replacing traditional production methods entirely. Short-form content has become increasingly important for studios seeking to engage audiences across social media platforms and streaming services where viewing habits differ from traditional long-form programming.

The announcement positions Lionsgate as among the more forward-leaning major studios in adopting AI technology for content creation, even as the entertainment industry continues to grapple with questions about how artificial intelligence will affect creative jobs and traditional production workflows. The studio's willingness to take an equity position signals confidence that AI-generated content will play a meaningful role in the future of entertainment production and distribution.

cards.headline: Larry David HBO Sketch Series Adds Isla Fisher and Jane Krakowski
cards.teaser: The upcoming HBO sketch show about American history will feature both actors in guest star roles.
cards.body:
Isla Fisher and Jane Krakowski will guest star in Larry David's upcoming HBO sketch series titled "Life, Larry, and the Pursuit of Unhappiness." The show explores American history through comedy.

David, the creator behind Seinfeld and Curb Your Enthusiasm, is venturing into sketch comedy with this new project. The series is set to air on HBO.

cards.headline: Pixar Announces Gatto, Animated Film About Italian Cats
cards.teaser: Mark Ruffalo and Laurence Fishburne will voice two cats in the studio's next animated feature set in Italy.
cards.body:
Pixar has announced Gatto, its next animated film featuring an all-star voice cast. Mark Ruffalo and Laurence Fishburne lend their voices to the feline characters Nero and Rocco respectively. The movie is set in Italy and explores a mobster-themed storyline.

The reveal comes shortly after Pixar's earlier success with Hoppers and just one week ahead of Toy Story 5's theatrical release. Pixar has already released a trailer introducing audiences to the Italian cat characters and the film's unique premise.

cards.headline: Raphael Bob-Waksberg Returns to Netflix With Long Story Short
cards.teaser: The creator's new animated series follows the Schwooper family across different years and decades.
cards.body:
Raphael Bob-Waksberg is returning to Netflix with an animated series called Long Story Short. The show centers on the Schwooper family—parents Naomi and Elliot and their children—as they navigate life's complexities. Bob-Waksberg previously created BoJack Horseman, the acclaimed Netflix animated series that ran for six seasons and gained recognition for its emotional storytelling and character development.

Long Story Short continues Bob-Waksberg's signature approach, delivering a family saga grounded in humanity and empathy.

cards.headline: Emmy Voting Opens With 555 Series Competing
cards.teaser: Television Academy members began casting ballots for the 2026 Primetime Emmy Awards nominations.
cards.body:
Voting for the 2026 Primetime Emmy Awards nominations has officially begun, with 555 series entering program categories. This represents a 7.5 percent decrease from last year's total. Nearly 24,000 Television Academy members divided among 31 peer groups now hold ballots.

The voting follows weeks of For Your Consideration events and studio campaigns. Academy members include directors, producers, and artisans who vote within their respective peer groups to determine which programs and performances will receive nominations.

cards.headline: Former Paramount President Jeff Shell Settles Lawsuit With Gambler
cards.teaser: Jeff Shell resolved litigation with R.J. Cipriani, who had sought $150 million for crisis PR work.
cards.body:
Jeff Shell, the former president of Paramount Skydance, has settled litigation with gambler R.J. Cipriani. Cipriani had accused Shell of leaking confidential company information and sued him, his wife, Paramount, and Larry and David Ellison in March.

Cipriani claimed he was owed millions for off-the-books crisis public relations work and had sought $150 million in his lawsuit. Shell had previously accused Cipriani of attempting a shakedown.

cards.headline: Alex Cooper's Unwell Signs Girls, Disrupted Podcast
cards.teaser: The podcast hosted by Georgia Hassarati and Isabel Timerman joins the Gen Z media company's network.
cards.body:
Georgia Hassarati and Isabel Timerman's podcast Girls, Disrupted has joined Alex Cooper's media company Unwell. The show will premiere its first episode under the new deal on Tuesday, June 16, rolling out across YouTube and major podcast platforms.

New episodes will air weekly. Unwell, Cooper's Gen Z-focused media venture, continues building its podcast lineup with content geared toward younger audiences, covering pop culture, relationships, and entertainment topics.

hero.headline: House Democrat pledges investigation into Vance role in Epstein response
hero.teaser: Rep. Robert Garcia said he would investigate Vice President Vance's involvement in White House actions related to Jeffrey Epstein.
hero.body:
Rep. Robert Garcia of California, the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, announced Thursday that he will investigate Vice President Vance's involvement in how the Trump administration has handled matters connected to Jeffrey Epstein, the convicted sex offender.

Garcia characterized the administration's response as a cover-up and said the committee would pursue answers about Vance's specific role. The House Oversight Committee, where Garcia holds the ranking Democratic position, has authority to examine activities within executive branch agencies.

The Democrat's statement came after the New York Times published a report claiming that Vance directed the White House's response to information related to Epstein. The nature of that information and the specific details of what the alleged cover-up entails were not immediately clear from Garcia's public comments.

This investigation represents one of several congressional inquiries into matters surrounding Epstein, the financier who died in jail in 2019 while awaiting trial on sex trafficking charges. He had previously pleaded guilty to soliciting prostitution from a minor in Florida.

The timing of Garcia's announcement reflects broader congressional interest in Epstein-related matters. Bill Gates recently testified before the House Oversight Committee in a closed-door session, telling lawmakers that he never witnessed evidence of Epstein engaging in criminal activity and that he supports the release of all Epstein-related files. Gates stated in his opening remarks that survivors of Epstein's crimes deserve justice.

Garcia's pledge to investigate represents a Democratic effort to scrutinize the new administration's handling of sensitive matters. As ranking member of the Oversight Committee, Garcia has significant authority to demand documents, schedule hearings, and compel testimony from administration officials.

The investigation will likely focus on what specific information about Epstein the White House responded to and what actions, if any, were taken. It remains unclear whether the investigation will examine communications between Vance and other officials, meetings held in response to Epstein-related matters, or documents the White House may have sought to control or suppress.

The House Oversight Committee has jurisdiction over federal agencies and executive branch activities, giving it the power to investigate how the Trump administration has approached matters connected to Epstein. Garcia's announcement suggests the committee intends to use that authority to examine whether proper procedures were followed and whether transparency was maintained.

The investigation could produce public hearings, written inquiries, or requests for documents from the White House. How the administration responds to such requests remains to be seen, particularly given the potential sensitivity of Epstein-related matters and their connection to various public figures.

Garcia's statement marks the beginning of what could become a significant point of contention between congressional Democrats and the Trump administration over handling of the Epstein case.

cards.headline: Trump threatens to seize Iranian oil hub as Graham and Johnson respond
cards.teaser: President Trump threatened to seize Kharg Island, Iran's primary oil export facility, in a social media post on Thursday morning.
cards.body:
President Trump threatened Thursday to seize Kharg Island, Iran's primary oil export facility, and launch further military strikes against Iran. In a Truth Social post, Trump said the US would hit Iran "very hard tonight" and take control of the island, which handles approximately 90% of Iran's oil exports and contains vast storage facilities.

Sen. Lindsey Graham endorsed the threat, calling it a potential game-changer that could force Iran to negotiate when combined with military pressure and sanctions. Speaker Mike Johnson offered a more cautious response, saying he wouldn't read too much into the details of Trump's statement and suggesting it was strategic communication aimed at adversaries in the region.

cards.headline: Rep. Nancy Mace vows to be more of a menace after primary defeat
cards.teaser: The South Carolina Republican responded to comedian Rob Schneider's message as her term nears its end.
cards.body:
Rep. Nancy Mace of South Carolina said on Thursday she would be more of a menace than ever as her congressional term winds down following her primary election loss. Mace made the statement on social platform X in response to comedian Rob Schneider, who praised her as the champion we didn't deserve.

Mace wrote that she never thought she would get her congressional send-off from Deuce Bigalow, referencing Schneider's role in the comedy film. The outgoing representative faces the end of her term after losing her primary race.

cards.headline: Judge acquits former NYC comptroller Lander in federal obstruction case
cards.teaser: The ruling comes in the final days of the primary campaign between Lander and Rep. Dan Goldman.
cards.body:
A judge found former New York City Comptroller Brad Lander not guilty in a federal obstruction case related to 26 Federal Plaza. The ruling was issued on Thursday as Lander campaigns in a primary race against Rep. Dan Goldman.

The case involved allegations of obstruction at the federal building in Manhattan. Lander previously served as the city's comptroller before entering the congressional primary race.

cards.headline: Rep. Jasmine Crockett defends Karmelo Anthony after Austin Metcalf killing
cards.teaser: The Texas Democrat made statements about Anthony, who killed Metcalf.
cards.body:
Rep. Jasmine Crockett of Texas defended Karmelo Anthony following the killing of Austin Metcalf. Anthony was convicted of murdering Metcalf.

Crockett's statements drew attention for her expressed sympathy toward Anthony. The case involved Anthony's conviction in Metcalf's death.

cards.headline: Universities accused of failing to protect Jewish students
cards.teaser: An analysis examines whether higher education institutions have kept their commitments to student safety.
cards.body:
Universities face scrutiny over whether they have fulfilled promises to protect Jewish students on campus. The examination looks at institutional responses to campus unrest and safety concerns.

The analysis frames the issue as extending beyond individual campus incidents. Critics argue that universities made commitments to student safety that they have not upheld.

cards.headline: Trump threatens to seize Iranian oil facilities
cards.teaser: The president said the US may take Kharg Island and other infrastructure in Iran.
cards.body:
President Trump said on Thursday that the United States would seize control of Iran's oil and gas infrastructure, specifically targeting Kharg Island. He also threatened additional military strikes against Iran that night, claiming most of Iran's offensive capacity had already been destroyed.

The escalation follows a second day of exchanges between U.S. and Iranian forces, despite a nominal ceasefire being in place. Kharg Island handles approximately 90% of Iran's oil exports and contains vast storage facilities, making it a strategically significant target in the ongoing conflict.
